The attacking team scores by moving through any scoring gate.
Defenders chase and attempt to force a turnover.
Defenders score by locking the football inside the square for five seconds or winning possession.
Reset with a new contest.
coachingPoints: Spread immediately once possession is controlled.
Avoid every midfielder chasing the same first handball.
Assign forward, lateral and release movement.
Accelerate into separate lanes.
The ball winner should scan before standing upright.
Outside receivers must adjust to the selected lane.
Maintain support behind the football.
Straighten the attack when the central lane is open.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether attackers separate immediately.
Whether midfielders occupy different lanes.
Whether the ball winner has multiple options.
Whether outside receivers adjust their position.
Whether the team retains support behind possession.
Whether forward movement begins before defenders recover.
progressions: Add another defender outside the square.
Require a kick to complete the scoring action.
successIndicators: Provide forward, lateral and release options.
Maintain support after the first disposal.
Reach a scoring gate before defenders recover.
matchApplication: Midfield possession can be wasted when teammates remain clustered around the contest. Immediate spread creates space, improves disposal angles and allows the team to attack before the opposition rebuilds its defensive structure.

title: Switch Runner Relay
primarySkill: Running to support a switch of play.
objective: Develop coordinated off-ball running during a switch so the receiving side has immediate forward, lateral and supporting options.
groundSize: A 55-metre-long by 50-metre-wide area divided into left, central and right channels.
setup:
Mark three vertical channels.
Use seven attackers against four defenders.
Begin possession in one outside channel.
Position two attackers in the central channel and two on the weak side.
Place a scoring gate at the far end of each outside channel.
Defenders begin compressed towards the ball side.
Weak-side attackers must hold until the switch is initiated.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with two or three possessions on the ball side.
A supporting player behind the football initiates the switch.
Central attackers move to create safe connecting options.
Weak-side attackers begin forward and lateral runs as the transfer starts.
The football is transferred through the central channel or by a safe long kick.
The weak-side receiver takes possession and assesses the available runners.
One runner presents forward, one provides support inside and one remains behind.
The attacking team scores by moving through the weak-side gate.
Defenders attempt to recover and close the new attacking lanes.
Rotate starting sides and roles after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Hold weak-side width until the switch begins.
Start support runs as the first transfer is made.
Do not wait until the football arrives on the far side.
Provide different movement angles around the receiver.
Central connections must remain safe.
The weak-side receiver should scan before possession.
Accelerate once the defence begins shifting.
Maintain one support option behind the switch.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether weak-side players hold their position.
Whether support runs begin at the correct time.
Whether the receiver has multiple options on arrival.
Whether central players create safe transfer angles.
Whether attackers accelerate against the moving defence.
Whether support remains behind possession.
progressions: Allow defenders to begin in a balanced structure.
Add another defender on the weak side.
Add a forward target beyond the scoring gate.
successIndicators: Provide several options around the receiver.
matchApplication: A switch creates an advantage only when players on the receiving side move with the transfer. This drill teaches weak-side players to time their runs so the switch becomes an attacking action rather than a slow change of possession.

title: Lead-Clear-Replace Movement
primarySkill: Rotating attacking players through lead, clear and replacement movements.
objective: Teach players to maintain attacking movement by clearing space after an unsuccessful lead and replacing the vacated position with a new option.
groundSize: A 45-metre-long by 35-metre-wide attacking area with three leading zones.
setup:
Mark three staggered leading zones.
Position three attackers inside the area.
Position two ball movers outside the area.
Add two defenders.
Assign one attacker to begin in each leading zone.
Use a scoring target or main goals.
Defenders may track leads but begin with controlled pressure.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball movers circulate possession outside the attacking area.
The first attacker leads towards the football.
If not used, the leader clears through or across the area.
A second attacker replaces the vacated zone.
The third attacker adjusts to maintain depth and width.
The ball carrier selects the best available lead.
The selected attacker marks or gathers and attempts to score or connect.
Unselected attackers continue the lead-clear-replace pattern.
Play continues for up to 20 seconds or until a score or turnover.
Rotate attackers, defenders and ball movers.
coachingPoints: A lead that is not used must clear space.
Replacement movement should begin as the first player clears.
Do not stop in the centre of the attacking area.
Maintain one deep option.
Communicate who is replacing each space.
The ball carrier should remain patient while movement develops.
Leads should be angled and purposeful.
Continue moving after the first entry.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether unused leaders clear the target area.
Whether replacement movement occurs immediately.
Whether attackers preserve depth.
Whether several players lead into the same space.
Whether ball carriers wait for a better option.
Whether movement continues after the first entry.
progressions: Continue play until a score or defensive exit.
regressions: Use fixed lead and replacement zones.
matchApplication: Attacking movement often stalls when a player leads, is ignored and remains in the same space. Lead-clear-replace rotation keeps the forward area active and creates repeated options for the ball carrier.

title: Rolling Attacking Grid
primarySkill: Maintaining attacking movement as possession travels through changing spaces.
objective: Develop continuous team movement in which players enter, leave and replace grid spaces as the football advances.
groundSize: A 60-metre-long by 45-metre-wide area divided into twelve equal grid sections.
setup:
Divide the area into a four-by-three grid.
Use nine attackers against six defenders.
Begin with attackers spread across the first three rows.
Place a scoring gate at the far end.
No more than two attackers may occupy one grid section.
After disposing, a player must enter a different section.
Defenders may move freely.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins possession in the first row.
Players move the football by kick or handball.
After disposing, each player must leave the current grid section.
Another attacker replaces the vacated section when useful.
Players ahead create width and depth across different sections.
Defenders attempt to intercept and compress space around the football.
Attackers score by progressing through the final row and scoring gate.
A turnover occurs if three attackers occupy one section or possession is held for longer than five seconds.
On turnover, defenders attack towards the opposite end.
Play continues for blocks of two to three minutes.
Rotate teams and restart from varied positions.
coachingPoints: Move into a new space after disposal.
Replace useful space rather than following the football.
Maintain players ahead, beside and behind possession.
Scan adjacent sections before moving.
Avoid filling every nearby grid.
Use quick movement to escape compressed areas.
Preserve connection across the full area.
React immediately when possession changes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether disposers enter new sections.
Whether vacated spaces are replaced intelligently.
Whether players maintain width and depth.
Whether attackers crowd the ball-side grids.
Whether the football moves away from defensive compression.
Whether teams transition immediately after turnovers.
regressions: Allow players to remain in a section for one extra possession.
Pause to rebuild the grid after turnovers.
successIndicators: Progress the football through multiple grid rows.
matchApplication: Australian football requires constant movement through changing spaces. This drill develops the ability to reposition collectively as possession advances rather than relying on fixed formations or following the football.

title: Team Offence Movement Assessment
primarySkill: Applying coordinated attacking movement in opposed play.
objective: Assess whether players can independently move, rotate and replace positions to maintain attacking connection during realistic opposed football.
groundSize: Three-quarter ground or full ground.
setup:
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Use three-quarter ground for smaller groups and full ground for larger squads.
Mark optional reference channels for the first assessment block.
Begin from varied situations including centre possession, defensive-half turnover, stoppage exit and boundary possession.
Use normal goals.
Assign coaches to observe movement after disposal, lane use, replacement movement and connection between lines.
Allow realistic legal contact.
Provide no coaching during the first block.
howTheDrillWorks:
Begin from a selected match scenario.
The team in possession attempts to move the football into attack and score.
Players must provide movement ahead, beside and behind possession.
Every disposer is expected to move again unless holding a deliberate structural role.
Players away from the football must rotate, replace or preserve space.
Normal match scoring applies.
Award one bonus point for each clearly successful movement action:
A give-and-go that breaks a line.
A third-player connection.
A coordinated switch with weak-side runners.
A lead-clear-replace sequence.
A midfield spread that creates forward progression.
The defending team attacks immediately after turnovers.
Play in blocks of four to six minutes.
Record observations without stopping the first block.
Provide targeted feedback between blocks.
Remove reference markings for the final block.
Complete the final block without coach intervention.
coachingPoints: Move immediately after disposal.
Exchange and replace positions with purpose.
Maintain width and depth.
Keep support staggered.
Create movement before the football arrives.
Preserve a player behind possession.
Use weak-side runners during switches.
Coordinate midfield and forward movement.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether disposers remain involved.
Whether players exchange lanes without crowding.
Whether third-player runs appear when direct lanes are closed.
Whether weak-side movement supports switches.
Whether midfielders spread after possession is won.
Whether forwards clear and replace space.
Whether attacking lines remain connected.
Whether movement continues under fatigue and pressure.
progressions: Increase defensive numbers around selected possessions.
Use full match rules and continuous play.
regressions: Pause between possessions for structural correction.
Assess one movement principle at a time.
successIndicators: Generate scoring opportunities through coordinated movement.
matchApplication: This assessment combines the movement principles developed through TO-021 to TO-029. It allows coaches to determine whether players can sustain coordinated attacking movement under realistic pressure without relying on fixed patterns or constant instruction.

title: Double-Support Exit
primarySkill: Providing two connected support options after possession exits congestion.
objective: Develop players’ ability to create an immediate forward option and a secondary release option after the football is won and moved outside pressure.
groundSize: A 40-metre-long by 30-metre-wide area with a central pressure zone and two forward support lanes.
setup:
Mark a central pressure square approximately 12 metres by 12 metres.
Mark two angled support lanes leading towards a scoring gate.
Place two attackers and two defenders inside the pressure square.
Position two attacking support players outside the square.
Position one defender between the support lanes.
Begin each repetition with a ground-ball feed or short contested possession.
Rotate inside players, support runners and defenders regularly.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players compete for possession inside the pressure square.
When an attacker wins the football, the first support player presents on a forward angle.
The second support player remains slightly wider or behind as a release option.
The ball winner disposes to the safest support player.
The receiver accelerates towards the scoring gate.
The unused support player adjusts to become the next option.
The original ball winner exits the pressure square and reconnects behind possession.
Defenders chase and attempt to force a turnover.
Attackers score by carrying or disposing through the gate.
Defenders score by intercepting or preventing the ball from exiting the square within five seconds.
Reset with a new contested feed.
coachingPoints: Provide two clearly different support angles.
The first option should attack forward space.
The second option should remain available if the forward lane closes.
Support runners must arrive as possession is secured.
The ball winner should protect the football before releasing.
The first receiver must continue moving.
Unused support players must reposition immediately.
The original ball winner must reconnect after disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether two distinct support options are available.
Whether runners time their movement correctly.
Whether the ball winner scans outside pressure.
Whether the first receiver maintains forward momentum.
Whether the unused support player becomes the next option.
Whether the original ball winner exits and supports.
progressions: Allow defenders to choose which support option to close.
Require attackers to complete a kick after exiting.
Continue live in the opposite direction after turnovers.
successIndicators: Continue forward after the first disposal.
Reconnect the original ball winner into the attacking chain.
matchApplication: Possession won in congestion becomes more effective when the ball carrier has more than one exit option. Double support prevents the defence from closing a single predictable lane and improves the team’s ability to continue attacking.

title: Delayed Outside Run
primarySkill: Timing a delayed outside support run.
objective: Teach outside players to preserve space and delay their movement until the ball carrier draws pressure and creates a clear release opportunity.
groundSize: Several lanes approximately 35 metres long and 12 metres wide.
setup:
Divide players into groups of three attackers and one defender.
Position the ball carrier in the centre of the lane.
Position one attacker ahead as a decoy or forward option.
Position the outside runner behind and near the boundary-side cone.
Place the defender five metres in front of the ball carrier.
Mark a scoring gate at the far end.
Rotate all roles after each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier moves towards the defender.
The forward attacker presents and draws the defender’s attention.
The outside runner holds position behind the football.
As the defender commits, the outside runner accelerates past the ball carrier.
The ball carrier releases by handball into the runner’s path.
The forward attacker turns and supports inside.
The outside runner continues towards the scoring gate.
The defender may chase once the handball is released.
Attackers score by reaching the gate under control.
Repeat from the opposite side.
coachingPoints: Hold width before beginning the run.
Delay until the defender commits.
Accelerate sharply rather than drifting forward.
Run outside the ball carrier’s shoulder.
Handball into the runner’s forward path.
The decoy forward should become an inside support option.
The original ball carrier should continue after disposal.
Avoid signalling the run too early.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the outside runner preserves space.
Whether the run begins after defensive commitment.
Whether the defender is genuinely drawn.
Whether the handball is delivered to advantage.
Whether inside support forms after the release.
Whether the original ball carrier remains involved.
progressions: Allow the defender to choose whether to close the forward or outside option.
Add a second defender near the gate.
Continue into a live three-versus-two attack.
regressions: Allow a loud verbal call from the runner.
successIndicators: Time the support run after defensive commitment.
matchApplication: Outside support is most damaging when it arrives after a defender has committed towards the ball carrier. Delayed movement preserves space and creates a clean line-breaking option.

title: Underlap Through the Inside Lane
primarySkill: Using an underlap run inside the player in possession.
objective: Develop players’ ability to attack an inside lane with a timed underlap when the defender protects the outside support route.
groundSize: Several lanes approximately 35 metres long and 14 metres wide, divided into inside and outside channels.
setup:
Position one ball carrier in the outside half of each lane.
Position one support runner behind and closer to the inside channel.
Place one defender ahead, initially shading towards the boundary side.
Position a second attacker further forward as a target.
Mark a central scoring gate at the far end.
Rotate roles after each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier advances along the outside half of the lane.
The defender protects the obvious outside run.
The support runner begins behind possession and accelerates through the inside lane.
The ball carrier draws the defender and handballs inside.
The underlap runner receives moving towards the central scoring gate.
The forward target leads away from the lane to create space.
The original ball carrier follows and provides outside support.
The defender chases after the release.
Attackers score by moving through the central gate.
Repeat from both sides of the area.
coachingPoints: Begin behind the football.
Attack the inside lane only when it is open.
Time the run as the defender shifts outside.
The ball carrier must recognise the defender’s body position.
Handball into the runner’s path.
The forward target should clear central space.
The original ball carrier should become the next outside option.
Maintain separation between the runner and ball carrier.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the runner begins behind possession.
Whether the defender’s positioning justifies the underlap.
Whether the run is timed after the defender moves outside.
Whether the forward target creates space.
Whether the handball leads the runner.
Whether support forms after the release.
progressions: Allow the defender to protect either lane.
Add a second defender near the scoring gate.
Allow the runner to choose overlap or underlap.
Continue into a live forward-entry phase.
successIndicators: Time the underlap after defensive movement.
Maintain support after the line break.
matchApplication: Defenders often anticipate outside overlap runs. An underlap attacks the space inside the ball carrier and can open the corridor when the opposition overprotects the boundary side.

title: Cross-Over Running Pair
primarySkill: Exchanging running lines to confuse and separate defenders.
objective: Teach pairs of attackers to cross running lines at different depths while preserving clear disposal lanes and avoiding congestion.
groundSize: A 40-metre-long by 30-metre-wide area with two outside starting lanes and a central finishing zone.
setup:
Position a ball carrier at one end.
Place two attackers ahead in separate outside lanes.
Position one defender between them.
Mark a central receiving zone further forward.
One attacker begins slightly deeper than the other.
Use several groups where possible.
Rotate all roles after each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier begins moving forward.
The two attackers start in separate lanes and at different depths.
The deeper attacker runs diagonally towards the opposite lane.
The higher attacker crosses later and moves into the space vacated by the first runner.
The defender must decide which runner to track.
The ball carrier selects the attacker who gains separation.
The selected receiver continues into the central finishing zone.
The unused attacker becomes the next support option.
Attackers score by completing possession inside the finishing zone.
Repeat with the opposite player beginning deeper.
coachingPoints: Begin at different depths.
Do not cross at the same point or time.
The first run should move the defender.
The second runner should attack the space created.
Maintain enough separation to preserve two disposal options.
The ball carrier should delay disposal until separation appears.
The unused runner must remain involved.
Communicate roles before movement begins.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether runners begin at different depths.
Whether crossing movements are staggered.
Whether the defender is forced to make a decision.
Whether the ball carrier waits for separation.
Whether disposal lanes remain clear.
Whether the unused runner supports the next action.
progressions: Allow runners to choose whether to cross.
Continue into a three-versus-two scoring action.
successIndicators: Continue support after the first possession.
matchApplication: Cross-over movement can separate defenders and open space when attackers coordinate their timing. The pattern is effective around half-forward, midfield and stoppage exits where defenders are tracking direct opponents.

title: Running Rotation Around the Mark
primarySkill: Rotating support runners around a player who has marked.
objective: Develop coordinated movement around a marked possession so the receiver has a run-past option, a forward lead and a safe release option.
groundSize: A 50-metre-long by 35-metre-wide area with three staggered marking stations.
setup:
Mark three receiving stations through the area.
Position one player at each station.
Place one support runner behind each station.
Position one forward leader beyond each station.
Begin the football at one end.
Use a second group in an adjacent channel where possible.
No defenders are used initially.
howTheDrillWorks:
The starting player kicks to the first receiver.
As the mark is taken, the rear support runner accelerates past on one side.
The forward player leads on the opposite side.
The marker scans both options.
The marker may handball to the run-past player or kick to the forward leader.
The unused player rotates into the position vacated by the selected option.
The original kicker moves forward to become the next release option.
The sequence repeats through all stations.
The group scores by completing the final possession through the end gate.
Reset from the opposite end.
coachingPoints: Movement should begin while the football is in flight.
Provide options on different sides of the marker.
The run-past player must begin behind possession.
The forward leader should create depth.
The marker should scan before completing the mark.
Unused players must rotate into useful positions.
The original kicker must advance after disposal.
Avoid all movement occurring on the same side.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether support movement begins early.
Whether options appear on different sides.
Whether the run-past player starts behind.
Whether the marker scans before possession.
Whether unused players rotate.
Whether the chain remains connected.
progressions: Add a passive defender at each station.
Allow defenders to close one option.
Continue live after a dropped mark.
successIndicators: Move while the football is in flight.
Maintain connection through the entire chain.
matchApplication: A marked possession should trigger immediate movement around the football. Coordinated rotation prevents the marker from becoming isolated and allows the team to continue attacking before defenders reset.

title: Continuous Forward Replacement
primarySkill: Replacing forward positions during continuous attacking movement.
objective: Teach players to replace vacated forward positions so the attacking structure remains connected as teammates lead, clear or rotate through the midfield.
groundSize: An area from the centre square to the goal square using the full attacking width.
setup:
Position three forwards inside 50.
Position three high forwards or midfielders outside 50.
Add four defenders.
Mark three reference zones: deep forward, high forward and midfield connection.
Begin the football near the centre.
Players may move freely between zones once the drill begins.
Use normal goals.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking group begins moving possession from midfield.
A high forward leads towards the football.
A deeper forward clears or rotates into another lane.
A midfielder advances to replace the vacated high-forward position.
The ball carrier selects the safest connection.
After disposal, players continue rotating through the three reference zones.
At least one attacker must remain inside the deep-forward zone.
At least one attacker must remain in the high connection zone.
Play continues until a score, turnover or defensive exit.
Reset with players beginning in different roles.
Rotate attackers and defenders after three repetitions.
coachingPoints: Replace positions as soon as they are vacated.
Maintain one deep target.
Maintain one high connection.
Do not allow all forwards to lead towards the football.
Midfielders should advance after releasing possession.
Communicate rotations early.
Clear space fully before another player enters it.
Continue movement after the first forward entry.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether vacated forward positions are replaced.
Whether one deep target remains.
Whether midfielders advance into connection roles.
Whether players crowd the same lane.
Whether rotations occur before the attack becomes disconnected.
Whether movement continues after the first entry.
regressions: Fix one player in the deep-forward zone.
successIndicators: Maintain deep and high attacking targets.
Sustain forward structure through continuous play.
matchApplication: Forward movement can create structural gaps when players lead away from goal and are not replaced. Continuous replacement ensures the team retains dangerous targets and connection points throughout the possession.

title: Wide-to-Inside Runner Exchange
primarySkill: Exchanging wide and inside running roles during attacking possession.
objective: Develop coordinated movement in which a wide player moves inside while an inside player replaces the vacated outside lane.
groundSize: A 50-metre-long by 40-metre-wide area divided into one inside lane and two outside lanes.
setup:
Mark a central inside lane and two outside lanes.
Use six attackers against three defenders.
Begin possession in one outside lane.
Position one attacker inside and another further ahead outside.
Position defenders to protect the central lane.
Mark a scoring gate at the far end.
Restart from alternating sides.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with possession in an outside lane.
The inside attacker moves towards the football and draws a defender.
The wide player ahead begins a diagonal run into the central lane.
The original inside attacker continues outward to replace the wide lane.
The ball carrier chooses between the inside runner and the replacement wide option.
The unused option adjusts to support the next disposal.
Attackers continue exchanging roles as possession advances.
The team scores by moving through the scoring gate.
Defenders score by intercepting or forcing the football outside the area.
Rotate roles after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Exchange roles rather than abandoning width.
The inside runner and wide replacement must move at different angles.
Begin the exchange as possession approaches.
The ball carrier should scan both options.
Preserve one outside option at all times.
The central runner should receive moving forward.
Unused players must continue supporting.
Communicate the exchange early.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the wide lane is replaced.
Whether inside and outside movements are coordinated.
Whether defenders are forced to choose.
Whether the central runner receives with forward momentum.
Whether the ball carrier scans both options.
Whether the shape remains balanced after the exchange.
progressions: Allow players to choose whether to exchange.
successIndicators: Force defenders to make a choice.
Preserve attacking balance after the exchange.
matchApplication: Wide and inside players frequently exchange positions to disrupt defensive match-ups. Effective rotation opens central space while ensuring the team still has an outside release option.

title: Support Run Decision Gate
primarySkill: Selecting the correct support run according to defender positioning.
objective: Develop players’ ability to choose whether to overlap, underlap, hold width or remain behind possession based on the defender’s movement.
groundSize: A 35-metre-long by 25-metre-wide area with four marked support gates.
setup:
Mark four support gates around the starting ball carrier:
Outside overlap gate.
Inside underlap gate.
Lateral width gate.
Rear release gate.
Use two attackers and one defender per group.
Position the support runner behind the ball carrier.
The defender begins ahead and may shade towards any gate.
Place a scoring gate at the far end.
Rotate roles after every repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier begins moving forward.
The defender selects a position that closes one or more support gates.
The support runner scans the defender’s position.
The runner chooses the most effective available movement:
Outside overlap.
Inside underlap.
Lateral width.
Rear release.
The ball carrier scans and decides whether to use the runner.
If used, the runner receives and attacks the scoring gate.
If not used, the runner adjusts and remains connected.
The defender becomes fully active after the first disposal.
Attackers score by reaching the gate under control.
Repeat with a new defender starting position.
coachingPoints: Read the defender before beginning the run.
Do not use the same support pattern every repetition.
Begin behind possession where possible.
Choose the space the defender has conceded.
Communicate without revealing the movement too early.
The ball carrier must still assess whether the disposal is safe.
Unused support should remain connected.
Accelerate decisively once the option is selected.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the runner scans the defender.
Whether the selected run matches the available space.
Whether players rely on one preferred pattern.
Whether the ball carrier recognises the same information.
Whether the runner remains useful if not selected.
Whether movement is decisive.
progressions: Continue into a live three-versus-two game.
regressions: Call the defender’s position before the repetition.
Reduce the number of possible support runs.
successIndicators: Select the support run suited to defender positioning.
matchApplication: Support running should respond to the defensive picture rather than follow a fixed pattern. Players who can select between overlap, underlap, width and release options are harder to defend and provide more reliable support.

title: Rotating Numbers-Up Attack
primarySkill: Maintaining attacking movement during a changing numerical advantage.
objective: Develop players’ ability to create, recognise and maintain a numerical advantage while rotating support roles around the football.
groundSize: A 50-metre-long by 40-metre-wide area divided into three horizontal zones.
setup:
Divide the area into three zones.
Use six attackers against four defenders.
Position two attackers and one defender in the first zone.
Position two attackers and two defenders in the middle zone.
Position two attackers and one defender in the final zone.
Players may move between zones after disposing.
Place a scoring gate at the far end.
On turnovers, defenders attack towards the opposite end.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with possession in the first zone.
After disposing forward, one attacker may run into the next zone.
The previous receiver or disposer must decide whether to advance, hold or support behind.
Attackers attempt to create a temporary numbers-up situation around the football.
Defenders may follow between zones after the football crosses.
Once possession reaches the final zone, attackers attempt to score through the gate.
If defenders win possession, roles reverse immediately.
The new attacking team attempts to create its own numerical advantage in the opposite direction.
Play continues for blocks of two to three minutes.
Award one bonus point when a team creates and successfully uses a clear numerical advantage.
coachingPoints: Run forward after disposal when it creates an advantage.
Do not advance every player and leave no support behind.
Recognise where the extra player is located.
Move the football before defenders recover.
Maintain width around the numerical advantage.
The unused player should become the next support option.
Communicate numbers and available space.
React immediately when possession changes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players recognise the current numbers.
Whether runners create useful rather than crowded advantages.
Whether one support player remains behind.
Whether the ball moves quickly enough to exploit the advantage.
Whether players rotate after disposal.
Whether transition occurs immediately after turnovers.
progressions: Require a kick to complete the scoring action.
Extend the activity to three-quarter ground.
regressions: Freeze defenders briefly after zone entry.
Pause to identify the numerical advantage.
matchApplication: Attacking advantages frequently appear and disappear as players run forward, defend or transition. Teams must recognise where the extra player is and use that advantage before the opposition reorganises.

title: Team Offence Running Patterns Assessment
primarySkill: Applying coordinated attacking running patterns under realistic pressure.
objective: Assess whether players can independently select, coordinate and execute effective attacking running patterns during opposed play.
groundSize: Three-quarter ground or full ground.
setup:
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Use three-quarter ground for smaller squads and full ground for larger groups.
Begin play from varied positions including stoppage exits, boundary possession, defensive-half turnover and controlled marks.
Use normal goals.
Assign coaches to observe support-run selection, positional replacement, spacing and movement after disposal.
Use optional reference lanes during the first block only.
Allow realistic legal contact appropriate to the playing group.
Provide no tactical instruction during the first assessment block.
howTheDrillWorks:
Begin from a selected match scenario.
The team in possession attempts to move the football into attack and score.
Players must select support runs according to defender positioning.
Disposers are expected to move again unless holding a deliberate structural role.
Players must replace vacated wide, inside, high-forward and deep-forward positions.
Normal match scoring applies.
Award one bonus point for each clearly effective running pattern:
A delayed outside overlap.
A successful underlap.
A cross-over movement that separates defenders.
A wide-to-inside exchange with outside replacement.
A numbers-up rotation used before defenders recover.
The defending team transitions immediately after turnovers.
Play in blocks of five to six minutes.
Coaches record observations without stopping the first block.
Provide targeted feedback between blocks.
Remove any reference lanes for the final block.
Complete a final block without coach intervention.
coachingPoints: Scan defender positioning before selecting a support run.
Begin support movement from behind or outside possession.
Use overlap, underlap, width or release according to available space.
Replace vacated positions immediately.
Maintain one option ahead and one behind possession.
Move the football quickly when numbers-up.
Continue running after disposal.
Preserve attacking structure when possession changes side.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players scan before moving.
Whether support runs suit the defensive picture.
Whether overlap and underlap movements are timed effectively.
Whether wide and inside positions are replaced.
Whether forward structure remains connected.
Whether players create and use numerical advantages.
Whether disposers continue supporting.
Whether movement remains organised under fatigue.
Whether players transition immediately after turnovers.
progressions: Increase defensive numbers in selected areas.
Use full match rules and continuous play.
regressions: Pause between possessions for positional correction.
Assess one running pattern at a time.
successIndicators: Select support runs according to defender positioning.
matchApplication: This assessment combines the movement principles developed through TO-031 to TO-039. It measures whether players can select and coordinate effective attacking running patterns without relying on fixed rehearsed sequences or constant coach direction.

title: Pressure Release to Width
primarySkill: Releasing possession from pressure into available width.
objective: Develop players’ ability to absorb controlled pressure, protect possession and release the football to a teammate positioned outside the defensive congestion.
groundSize: A 40-metre-long by 30-metre-wide area with a central pressure zone and two outside release lanes.
setup:
Mark a central pressure zone approximately 12 metres by 12 metres.
Mark one release lane on each side.
Place three attackers and three defenders inside the pressure zone.
Position one attacking receiver in each outside lane.
Place a scoring gate 15 metres beyond the pressure zone.
Begin each repetition with a ground-ball feed or short contested possession.
Rotate inside and outside players regularly.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players compete for possession inside the pressure zone.
The attacking team attempts to secure the football under controlled contact.
Outside receivers hold their width and communicate the available release side.
The ball carrier protects possession and scans outside.
The football is released by handball or short kick to the safest receiver.
The outside receiver accelerates towards the scoring gate.
Inside attackers exit the pressure zone and provide follow-up support.
Defenders chase once the release disposal is completed.
Attackers score by carrying or disposing through the gate.
Defenders score by intercepting or holding possession inside the zone for five seconds.
Reset with a new feed.
coachingPoints: Protect possession before attempting the release.
Outside players must remain clear of congestion.
Scan before the football is secured where possible.
Release to the side with the least defensive pressure.
Deliver the football into the receiver’s path.
Outside receivers should arrive moving rather than wait flat-footed.
Inside attackers must reconnect after the first disposal.
Avoid forcing a release through a covered lane.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball carrier protects possession effectively.
Whether outside players remain available.
Whether the release side is identified before pressure closes.
Whether the disposal allows continued movement.
Whether inside attackers reconnect.
Whether defenders force hurried or predictable releases.
progressions: Allow defenders to close one release lane.
Require a kick after the initial release.
Continue live in both directions after turnovers.
successIndicators: Convert the release into forward movement.
matchApplication: Teams must often absorb pressure around a contest before moving the football into space. Effective outside release allows contested possession to become attacking possession rather than another congested disposal.

title: Contact and Release Chain
primarySkill: Maintaining an attacking disposal chain through controlled contact.
objective: Teach players to remain composed through controlled contact and release possession to connected support without losing attacking momentum.
groundSize: A 35-metre-long by 20-metre-wide channel with three contact stations.
setup:
Mark three staggered contact stations through the channel.
Position one defender or pad holder at each station.
Divide attackers into groups of four.
Begin the football with the first attacker.
Position support runners behind and beside possession.
Mark a scoring gate at the far end.
Rotate contact roles regularly.
howTheDrillWorks:
The first attacker carries towards the opening contact station.
The defender applies controlled body pressure.
The ball carrier protects possession and releases to a support runner.
The receiver continues towards the next contact station.
The previous disposer follows and becomes the next support option.
The sequence repeats through all three stations.
Support players must remain on different angles.
The group scores by reaching the final gate without a fumble or turnover.
Defenders may increase pressure gradually as technique improves.
Rotate all roles after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Lower the centre of gravity before contact.
Keep the football away from the defender.
Maintain balance through the contact.
Release before the tackle becomes complete.
Support players should remain visible.
The disposer must continue running.
Communicate the next support option early.
Avoid blind or backward handballs.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball carrier braces safely.
Whether possession remains protected.
Whether support players maintain clear angles.
Whether the release occurs before control is lost.
Whether the disposer follows the football.
Whether technique remains composed under repeated contact.
progressions: Replace pads with controlled live defenders.
Add a second defender at the final station.
Require players to choose between two support options.
Continue into a live scoring action.
successIndicators: Maintain execution across repeated contact efforts.
matchApplication: Attacking possession frequently continues through tackles, bumps and body pressure. Players must protect the football and release to support before the defence can create a stoppage or turnover.
relatedDrills: TK-120 – Tackling and Pressure Chapter Final Assessment

title: Congested Three-Way Exit
primarySkill: Selecting the best exit from a congested possession.
objective: Develop players’ ability to identify whether the safest attacking exit is forward, lateral or behind when possession is won in congestion.
groundSize: A 35-metre by 35-metre area with one central contest zone and three exit gates.
setup:
Mark a central contest zone approximately 12 metres by 12 metres.
Place one forward gate, one lateral gate and one rear gate around the zone.
Position three attackers and three defenders inside.
Position one attacking support player beyond each gate.
Add one roaming defender outside the zone.
Begin with a ground-ball or stoppage feed.
Rotate inside and outside roles regularly.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players contest possession inside the central zone.
The outside defender positions to close one of the three exits.
The ball winner scans forward, lateral and rear options.
Outside attackers communicate and adjust their position.
The ball carrier selects the safest available exit.
The receiver takes possession and attempts to connect with another outside attacker.
Inside attackers leave the contest and support the next phase.
Attackers score one point for exiting cleanly and a second point for completing the next disposal.
Defenders score by intercepting or forcing a stoppage.
Reset with the roaming defender closing a different exit.
coachingPoints: Scan all exits before committing.
Forward is preferred only when it is safe.
Lateral release can create width.
Rear release can preserve possession and reset.
Outside players must remain visible.
The ball winner should avoid turning blindly.
Support must continue after the first exit.
Communicate which exit is open.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball winner scans all three exits.
Whether support players adjust to defensive movement.
Whether players force forward possession.
Whether the selected exit improves the attacking position.
Whether inside players support after release.
Whether the second disposal is completed.
progressions: Continue live after the second disposal.
regressions: Call the closed gate before the feed.
matchApplication: Congested possession rarely provides one automatic solution. Players must recognise when to attack forward, release laterally or move backwards to retain the football and rebuild the attacking phase.

title: Compressed-Space Possession Escape
primarySkill: Escaping defensive compression through coordinated short possession.
objective: Teach players to use short connected disposals and coordinated movement to escape a heavily compressed defensive area.
groundSize: A 25-metre by 25-metre square with four outside escape gates.
setup:
Mark four small escape gates around the outside of the square.
Use six attackers against four defenders.
Begin all players inside the central square.
Place one attacking target beyond each escape gate.
Defenders begin compact around the football.
Start with a coach feed to an attacker.
Rotate defenders after each two-minute block.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with possession inside the compressed area.
Attackers use handball and short movement to retain possession.
Players may not remain stationary for longer than three seconds.
Defenders attempt to intercept, tackle or force a stoppage.
Attackers attempt to draw defenders towards one side.
When an escape gate opens, the football is released to the outside target.
One or more attackers exit through the same or adjacent gate to support.
Attackers score one point for a clean escape and another point for completing a disposal beyond the square.
Defenders score for a turnover or five-second stoppage.
Restart immediately after each outcome.
coachingPoints: Keep support close enough to connect but not so close that one defender covers two players.
Move defenders before attempting the escape.
Use quick hands without rushing technique.
Reposition immediately after disposal.
Protect the football before releasing.
Recognise when an outside gate opens.
Accelerate after escaping.
Avoid repeated handballs that do not shift the defence.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players create useful short support angles.
Whether possession shifts the defenders.
Whether attackers recognise the open gate.
Whether handballs remain controlled.
Whether players accelerate after escape.
Whether repeated disposals improve or worsen the attacking position.
progressions: Continue into live transition after escape.
matchApplication: Teams are often compressed against the boundary or around a stoppage. Coordinated short possession can move the defensive pressure and create an escape route into open space.

title: Pressure Switch Decision
primarySkill: Deciding whether to switch play under defensive pressure.
objective: Develop players’ ability to recognise whether pressure should be escaped through a switch, a reset or continued possession on the original side.
groundSize: A 55-metre-long by 50-metre-wide area divided into ball-side, central and weak-side channels.
setup:
Use nine attackers against six defenders.
Begin possession in one outside channel.
Position defenders in a variable shape selected by the coach.
Position attacking support behind the football and across the weak side.
Mark one scoring gate at the end of each outside channel.
The defending shape may overcommit, remain balanced or disguise pressure.
Restart from alternating sides.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins under pressure in the ball-side channel.
Defenders attempt to close forward options.
Attackers assess the defensive shape.
The team may:
Continue safely down the original side.
Reset behind possession.
Transfer through central support.
Complete a full switch to the weak side.
Weak-side players hold width until the switch is initiated.
Attackers score two points for selecting and executing the best available solution.
They score one point for reaching either end gate.
Defenders score two points for intercepting a forced switch.
After each repetition, the coach briefly identifies whether the chosen solution matched the defensive picture.
Rotate defenders after three repetitions.
coachingPoints: Do not switch simply because the drill provides the option.
Scan defender numbers across the ground.
Use support behind possession when the direct switch is unsafe.
Maintain weak-side width.
Continue ball-side if that remains the best attacking route.
Transfer quickly once the switch decision is made.
Avoid slow possession that allows the defence to reset.
Communicate the selected direction across the team.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players assess defensive balance.
Whether switches are attempted through safe connections.
Whether weak-side players preserve space.
Whether the team recognises when continuing ball-side is better.
Whether the reset changes the attacking picture.
Whether decisions are executed collectively.
progressions: Allow defenders to change shape during play.
regressions: Tell attackers the defensive shape before each repetition.
matchApplication: Switching play can release pressure, but it can also create dangerous turnovers when used without scanning. Teams must understand when to switch, when to reset and when to continue through the original side.

title: Contested Mark Release
primarySkill: Supporting and releasing possession after a contested mark.
objective: Teach teammates to position for the mark, spill or immediate release so a contested aerial possession can continue into attack.
groundSize: A 40-metre-long by 30-metre-wide area with an aerial contest zone and forward scoring gate.
setup:
Position one attacker and one defender inside the aerial contest zone.
Position two attacking support players around the contest.
Position one defensive ground-level player.
Place a feeder 20–25 metres away.
Mark a scoring gate 15 metres beyond the contest.
Rotate aerial, ground-level and feeder roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder kicks to the aerial contest.
The attacker and defender compete for the football.
One support player positions front and centre.
The second support player positions outside or behind the contest.
If the attacker marks, support players present for immediate release or protected possession.
If the football spills, ground-level players compete to win it.
The attacking group attempts to release towards the scoring gate.
Defenders attempt to intercept or lock the football in.
Attackers score for a clean mark-and-release or spill recovery followed by a successful exit.
Rotate roles after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Support the likely drop zone, not the player’s back.
Maintain front-and-centre coverage.
Keep one outside release option.
The marker should scan before landing where possible.
Protect the mark before playing on.
Ground-level players must react to the actual spill.
Avoid all support players entering the aerial contest.
Continue forward once possession is released.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether ground-level support is balanced.
Whether attackers crowd the aerial contest.
Whether the marker scans and protects possession.
Whether players react quickly to a spill.
Whether the release option remains visible.
Whether possession becomes forward movement.
progressions: Continue into a live forward entry.
successIndicators: Continue the attacking phase after the contest.
matchApplication: A contested mark attempt does not end the attacking phase. Teams need ground-level coverage and immediate release options so both marks and spills can be converted into continued possession.

title: Spoil Recovery Attack
primarySkill: Recovering an attacking possession after a defensive spoil.
objective: Develop the attacking team’s ability to anticipate a spoil, recover the loose football and create a second scoring opportunity.
groundSize: A forward-50 area or a 45-metre-long by 40-metre-wide attacking zone.
setup:
Position one forward and one defender for an aerial contest.
Position three attacking ground-level players around the expected drop zone.
Position two defensive ground-level players.
Place a feeder outside the attacking area.
Use normal goals or a scoring gate.
Rotate aerial and ground-level roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder kicks to the forward contest.
The defender attempts to spoil towards a nominated or natural direction.
Attacking ground-level players position front and centre, goal side and outside.
Players react to the actual spoil.
The attacking team attempts to win the ground ball.
The first possessor may shoot, release to a teammate or reset outside pressure.
Defenders attempt to win possession and exit through a wide gate.
Attackers score normal match points.
An additional point is awarded for recovering the spoil and creating a controlled shot.
Rotate roles after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Expect the spoil rather than assuming the mark will be taken.
Cover different ground-level positions.
React to the football’s actual direction.
The first ground-ball player should secure possession.
Nearby attackers provide release options.
Avoid every player collapsing onto the loose football.
Apply immediate pressure if defenders recover.
Select the best scoring method after the recovery.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether attackers balance around the contest.
Whether players react rather than guess.
Whether one player attacks the football cleanly.
Whether support remains outside congestion.
Whether the recovery creates a quality scoring chance.
Whether forward pressure follows a defensive win.
progressions: Continue live until a score or defensive exit.
successIndicators: Create a controlled second scoring opportunity.
Apply pressure after a defensive recovery.
matchApplication: Many forward entries are spoiled rather than marked. Strong attacking teams anticipate this outcome, recover the loose football and create repeat scoring opportunities before defenders can exit.
relatedDrills: SP-080 – Spoiling and Aerial Defence Chapter Final Assessment
GB-120 – Ground Balls Chapter Final Assessment

title: Forward Contest Numbers
primarySkill: Creating and using a numerical advantage around a forward contest.
objective: Teach attackers to position around a forward contest so the team can exploit an extra player before defenders recover.
groundSize: A 50-metre-long by 45-metre-wide forward-half area.
setup:
Use seven attackers against five defenders.
Position one attacker and one defender in a deeper aerial contest.
Position remaining players across high-forward and ground-level roles.
Begin the football 50–60 metres from goal.
Defenders may vary between aerial support and ground-level coverage.
Use normal goals.
Rotate teams after four possessions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with possession outside 50.
Attackers assess where the numerical advantage exists.
The ball carrier may enter to the aerial contest, use the free high forward or retain possession.
Ground-level attackers organise around the likely contest.
If the football comes to ground, attackers attempt to identify and use the free player.
Defenders attempt to spoil, win possession and exit through wide gates.
Attackers score normal match points.
A bonus point is awarded when the extra attacker is used to create a shot.
Defenders receive two points for a clean exit.
Reset from a different starting angle.
coachingPoints: Identify the free attacker before the entry.
Do not send the extra player into the same aerial contest.
Position the extra player where they can receive or affect the next disposal.
Balance aerial and ground-level roles.
Use width if defenders collapse around the contest.
Attackers must communicate where the advantage exists.
Create a shot before defenders recover.
Apply pressure if the numerical advantage is lost through turnover.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether attackers identify the numerical advantage.
Whether the extra player remains outside congestion.
Whether forward entry matches the attacking numbers.
Whether ground-level roles are balanced.
Whether the free player is used quickly.
Whether defenders are prevented from exiting easily.
progressions: Begin from transition rather than controlled possession.
Continue live to the opposite goal after turnovers.
successIndicators: Preserve space around the forward contest.
Use the free player before defenders recover.
matchApplication: A numerical advantage inside the forward half is valuable only when attackers recognise and use the free player. Poor spacing can remove that advantage by drawing everyone into the same contest.

title: Pressure Forward Entry Choice
primarySkill: Selecting a forward-entry option under immediate pressure.
objective: Develop players’ ability to choose between a direct entry, short connection, lateral release or reset when pressured near attacking 50.
groundSize: An area from approximately 70 metres from goal to the goal line using full attacking width.
setup:
Use eight attackers against six defenders.
Position three attackers around the high-forward area and three deeper forwards.
Position one attacking reset player behind possession.
Begin the football 55–70 metres from goal.
Place one defender near the ball carrier to apply immediate pressure.
Remaining defenders organise inside the forward area.
Use normal goals.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with possession outside 50.
Immediate pressure is applied to the ball carrier.
Forwards provide varied short, deep and lateral options.
The ball carrier must choose between:
Direct forward entry.
Short high-forward connection.
Lateral release.
Reset behind possession.
The attack continues until a score, turnover or defensive exit.
A quality entry that creates a controlled shot earns one bonus point.
A forced entry intercepted by defenders gives them two points.
Defenders attempt to exit through wide gates after turnovers.
Reset from a different angle.
Rotate pressure defenders and attacking roles.
coachingPoints: Scan before taking possession.
Recognise the position of the pressure defender.
Do not kick long simply because forward pressure arrives.
Use the short connection if deeper options are covered.
Lateral release can improve the entry angle.
Reset if the entire forward area is outnumbered.
Forwards must provide different types of movement.
Deliver the football to advantage.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ball carrier scans early.
Whether pressure causes rushed long kicks.
Whether forward movement provides varied options.
Whether the reset player remains available.
Whether the chosen entry creates a scoring chance.
Whether defenders are punished for overcommitting.
progressions: Increase pressure around the ball carrier.
Allow defenders to change shape late.
regressions: Pause after the ball carrier receives.
successIndicators: Select an entry suited to the defensive picture.
Use short and lateral options effectively.
Retain possession when no safe entry exists.
matchApplication: Forward entries are frequently delivered under pressure. Effective attackers maintain composure, recognise available options and avoid giving defenders easy intercept opportunities through rushed disposal.

title: Pressure and Contest Offence Assessment

Begin possessions from varied contested situations including ground balls, stoppages, aerial contests, boundary pressure and pressured forward entries.
Use normal goals.
Mark optional wide defensive-exit gates.
Assign coaches to observe contest exit, support angles, decision quality, forward structure and transition.
Apply legal match-like contact appropriate to the playing group.
Provide no coaching during the opening assessment block.
howTheDrillWorks:
Begin each possession from a selected contested scenario.
The team that wins possession attempts to establish attacking structure and score.
Players must create forward, lateral and rear support around pressure.
The attacking team may release wide, reset, switch, attack centrally or continue through the original side.
Normal match scoring applies.
Award one bonus point for:
A clean release from congestion.
A composed disposal through contact.
Correct selection of forward, lateral or rear exit.
Recovery of a spoil followed by a controlled scoring chance.
Use of a numerical advantage around a forward contest.
The defending team attacks immediately after turnovers.
Play in blocks of five to six minutes.
Coaches record observations without stopping the first block.
Provide targeted feedback between blocks.
Change the contested starting scenario for each block.
Complete a final match-like block without coach intervention.
coachingPoints: Secure possession before attacking.
Protect the football through contact.
Provide support outside congestion.
Scan forward, lateral and behind.
Maintain width and depth under pressure.
Avoid rushed forward entries.
Use numerical advantages before defenders recover.
React immediately when possession changes.

Whether players remain composed under contact.
Whether support remains outside congestion.
Whether ball carriers scan multiple exits.
Whether skill execution remains reliable.

Whether aerial contests have ground-level support.
Whether numerical advantages are recognised.
Whether forward entries suit the defensive shape.
Whether transition response is immediate.

title: Boundary Pressure Escape
primarySkill: Escaping attacking pressure near the boundary.
objective: Develop players’ ability to retain possession near the boundary and create a safe release back towards open field.

setup:
Mark a boundary channel approximately eight metres wide along one side of the area.
Mark a wider inside channel leading towards a scoring gate.
Use six attackers against four defenders.
Begin the football inside the boundary channel.
Position one attacking support player behind possession and two inside the ground.
Defenders begin between the football and the inside channel.
Place a scoring gate at the far end of the inside channel.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins under pressure in the boundary channel.
The ball carrier protects possession and scans for support.
One attacker provides a short option behind the football.
Inside attackers move at different depths to create separate escape angles.
Attackers may use short possession along the boundary before attempting to escape.
The football is released inside when a safe lane opens.
Once possession reaches the inside channel, attackers accelerate towards the scoring gate.
Defenders attempt to trap the football against the boundary or intercept the inside release.
Attackers score two points for escaping inside and progressing through the gate.
They score one point for retaining possession safely along the boundary for six disposals.
Defenders score two points for a turnover or forced boundary exit.
Restart from the opposite side after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Protect the football from boundary-side pressure.
Maintain a player behind possession.
Inside options should remain separated at different depths.
Avoid attempting the inside release before defenders have been moved.

Continue supporting behind the first inside possession.

Allow defenders to transition after turnovers.

title: Forward Surge from Ground Ball
primarySkill: Creating immediate forward movement after winning a ground ball.

groundSize: A 45-metre-long by 30-metre-wide area with a ground-ball zone and three forward lanes.

Mark a ground-ball zone approximately 10 metres by 10 metres.
Mark three forward lanes beyond the zone.
Place two attackers and two defenders around the ground ball.
Position three attacking support players beyond or beside the contest.
Position one defensive sweeper further forward.
Place a scoring gate at the far end.
Begin each repetition with a rolling or bouncing football.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players compete to win the ground ball.
The nearest attacker attacks the football with body protection.
Supporting attackers spread into forward, lateral and rear positions.
The ball winner may carry, handball or release backwards before the team surges forward.
Once possession exits the ground-ball zone, support runners accelerate through separate lanes.
The defensive sweeper attempts to close the most direct route.
Attackers score by moving through any scoring gate.
Defenders score by winning possession or stopping forward movement for five seconds.
The original ball winner must continue supporting after disposal.
Rotate contest, support and sweeper roles after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Attack the football with speed and a low body position.
Protect the football before standing upright.
Support players should spread as possession is secured.
Create one direct option, one lateral option and one release option.
Use the first clean disposal rather than holding possession unnecessarily.
Continue running after releasing the football.
Exploit the moment before defenders recover.
Select the lane with the strongest numerical or spatial advantage.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ground-ball player protects possession.
Whether support spreads rather than collapsing.
Whether the first disposal is clean and purposeful.
Whether players enter separate forward lanes.
Whether the ball winner remains involved.
Whether attackers exploit the defensive recovery period.
